dedupe_keys.name: mwater free data platform and water point data for water sanitation and hygiene wash

description: mWater runs a free, cloud-based data management platform that governments, water utilities, service providers and NGOs use to collect, analyse and share data on water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) services and infrastructure. The Surveyor mobile app (Android, iOS and web) collects survey data, maps infrastructure and manages services online or offline; the data portal builds forms, maps and dashboards to share with partners and the public, with a library of standard forms and indicators and a Sanitation Asset Standard for sanitation assets. mWater reports over 390,000 user accounts in 199 countries and territories and 51.1 million survey responses, and says there is a wealth of open-access water resources data from its users. National systems built on it include the WASH monitoring system of Papua New Guinea's Department of National Planning and Monitoring, Uganda's RUMIS for water asset mapping and service monitoring, and Zimbabwe's environmental health information system. Coverage: global, as contributed by users. Format and access: all platform features are free for unlimited use after sign-up; users own their data, decide what to share and can download it at any time; an authenticated MCP server and API are listed at api.mwater.co. Licence: users own their data; the licence of public data and the terms of use were not read. Caveats: public data depend on what each organisation chooses to share, and what is openly downloadable without an account was not checked. Simulation uses: water point and sanitation asset inventories with functionality surveys for service continuity and emergency planning. Related records: the Water Point Data Exchange (data-wpdx-water-point-data-exchange) and the WHO/UNICEF JMP database (data-who-unicef-jmp-wash-database).
